chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: Do not write 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful' at the beginning of the letter to so-and-so, and there is no harm in writing it on the back of the letter to so-and-so.

key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for writing 'Bismillah' in letters according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the etiquette of Islamic correspondence by distinguishing between the formal invocation of God's name at the beginning of a letter and its placement on the reverse. It reflects the scholarly tradition of maintaining reverence for the Basmala while allowing practical flexibility in letter formatting, ensuring the divine name is not treated casually within the body of personal communication.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Hassan Bin Al Sarry, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Do not write ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful’ to so and so, and there is no problem if you were to write upon the back of the letter to so and so’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Hassan ibn al-Sari from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Do not write, ‘(I begin) in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful,’ ‘for so and so’ (in a letter), but it is not an offense to write at the back of the letter, ‘for so and so’.’”
